entities.summary:
Antoine de Gramont, 4th Duke of Gramont, Duke of Guiche, was a Marshal of France.

Born in 1695, Antoine de Gramont was the son of François I de Gramont, 3rd Duke of Gramont, and Anne de Lorraine. He inherited the titles of Duke of Guiche and Earl of Shrewsbury at the age of 25. In 1715, he married Anne de Montmorency, daughter of Louis II de Montmorency, 2nd Duke of Luxembourg.

Gramont played a significant role in the War of the Spanish Succession, serving as a Marshal of France and leading the French army to several victories. He was instrumental in the Battle of Blenheim, where the French were defeated by a coalition of British and Bavarian forces. Despite this defeat, Gramont's military skills and strategic thinking earned him recognition and respect from his peers.

Gramont's legacy extends beyond his military achievements. He was a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Catholic Church. He also played a key role in the development of the French nobility, serving as a member of the Conseil d'État and the Académie française.

Gramont died on September 16, 1725, at the age of 30, due to complications from a fever. His early death was a shock to the French nobility, and he was remembered as a brilliant and talented young leader.

Gramont's impact on French history was significant, shaping the country's military and political landscape for generations to come. His legacy continues to be felt today, with many historians and scholars recognizing his importance as a Marshal of France and a key figure in the War of the Spanish Succession.
